method_card.title: Quadratic Formula and Completing the Square
steps: Read a, b, c from \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), keeping signs.
Discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac\): positive gives 2 roots, zero gives 1, negative gives none.
Formula: \(x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\), dividing the whole top by 2a.
Completing the square: halve b, subtract its square. Form \((x+p)^2+q\) has turning point \((-p, q)\).
method_card.content: Two tools for quadratics that will not factorise. The discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac\) tells you how many real roots exist before you solve. The formula then finds them. Completing the square rewrites \(x^2 + bx + c\) as \((x + p)^2 + q\), which reveals the turning point and minimum value directly.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Read a, b and c, work out the discriminant b² − 4ac, and complete the square on simple x² + bx.
problem_bank.silver_description: Solve with the quadratic formula to 2 d.p., complete the square with a constant, and read turning points.
problem_bank.gold_description: Complete the square when a ≠ 1, use the discriminant as a condition (equal roots), and find minimum values.

worked_examples.question: Solve x^2 + 6x + 2 = 0 using the formula. Give answers to 2 d.p.
Write x^2 + 8x + 3 in the form (x + a)^2 + b

bronze.title: Bronze: a, b, c, the discriminant, and simple squares
steps: Every quadratic \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) hands you three numbers: a, b and c. Read them off, keeping every minus sign.
The discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac\). Its sign counts the roots: positive gives 2, zero gives 1, negative gives none.
To complete the square on \(x^2 + bx\): halve b, then subtract the square of that half. So \(x^2 + 6x = (x+3)^2 - 9\).

silver.title: Silver: the quadratic formula and completed squares
steps: When a quadratic will not factorise, use \(x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\). Work out the discriminant, then its square root.
The \(\pm\) gives two answers: + for the larger root, − for the smaller. Divide the whole top by \(2a\), not just part of it.
Completing the square \(x^2 + bx + c = (x + p)^2 + q\) puts the turning point at \((-p, q)\) with no extra work.

gold.title: Gold: harder squares and the discriminant as a condition
steps: When \(a \neq 1\), factor a out of the first two terms first: \(2x^2 + 8x = 2(x^2 + 4x)\), then complete the square inside.
The discriminant is also a condition: equal roots means \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\). Set it to zero and solve for the unknown.
The completed form \(a(x + p)^2 + q\) gives the minimum value \(q\) straight away, reached at \(x = -p\).
